title: Pilot roadmap — Telemetry & KPI calibration notebook
content:
Purpose:
A compact working notebook to calibrate telemetry, acceptance thresholds, and rollout staging for the Q1 pilot (internal beta) of the new embeddings+chat routing feature. This is intentionally pragmatic: mix of rough math, guardrails, and queries we can paste into dashboards/alerts.

TL;DR (one paragraph):
We will run a 4-stage ramp (0.5% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%) over three weeks. Primary success criteria: p95 latency < 350ms (model path), error rate < 1.0% sustained, per-request cost within +12% of baseline. Canary pass requires 48h of stable telemetry at each stage with no critical rollbacks. If any safety/regression signals trigger, immediately pause and escalate to the oncall + product ops lead.

Important context / constraints:
- Target workload: customer-facing chat where 60% requests hit the embeddings+rerank path, average tokens in = 120, out = 80.
- Dedicated capacity pool available: 8xA100-equivalent GPUs in the pilot region.
- Baseline (control): hosted-chat-v2 (current production) metrics for comparison.
- Measured cold-start variance observed on small traffic slices (~+40% p95) in previous experiments -> watch warmup.

KPI table (working numbers):
Metric | Control baseline | Pilot target | Alert threshold | Notes
---------------------------------------------------------------
p50 latency (ms) | 90 | <= 140 | N/A | per-route, measure model-only path
p95 latency (ms) | 220 | <= 350 | > 500 (5m sustained) -> page
error rate (5m) | 0.6% | <= 1.0% | > 1.5% (5m) -> page
request cost delta | 0% | <= +12% | > +25% vs baseline -> review
quality regressions (eval set) | N/A | no regressions | regression > 2% accuracy drop -> block
throughput (req/s) | 200 | support 600 | drop > 15% sustained -> investigate
cache hit rate | 18% | >= 30% | < 12% -> perf risk

Threshold notes: alert thresholds are intentionally conservative for pilot; production thresholds (post-pilot) will tighten. The error rate alert will be paired with a ‘dominant failure class’ tag so we can quickly triage (timeout vs model-run vs routing).

Staged rollout plan (timeline + acceptance):
Stage A — 0.5% (sanity) | Duration: 12–24h monitored
- Acceptance: no critical alerts, p95 < 2x baseline, errors < 2%
- Tasks: smoke tests, run the synthetic prompt set (10k prompts) against pilot routing stack

Stage B — 5% (warm traffic) | Duration: 48h
- Acceptance: 48h with all KPIs within target and no persistent errors
- Tasks: enable latency heatmaps, start cost telemetry (token-level), validate KV/prefix cache warmup

Stage C — 25% (operational validation) | Duration: 72h
- Acceptance: 72h stable, run ramp stress test to +40% peak for 30 minutes without SLO breach
- Tasks: autoscaling policy watch, canary slow-path simulation, enable detailed trace sampling (1%)

Stage D — 100% | Duration: final cutoff window 24h then full handoff
- Acceptance: stable 24h then schedule debrief and SLA signoff
- Tasks: finalize runbook, shift ops ownership to SRE, consolidate dashboards

Monitoring probes & example queries (copy-paste):
- p95 latency (PromQL-like):
  histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))
- error rate (ratio):
  sum(rate(requests_total{job="pilot-route",status!~"2.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(requests_total{job="pilot-route"}[5m]))
- cold-starts per minute (tagged runs):
  increase(model_process_start_total{route="pilot"}[10m])
- cache effectiveness:
  sum(increase(cache_hit_total[15m])) / sum(increase(cache_lookup_total[15m]))
- cost burn (token units):
  sum(rate(tokens_consumed_total{route="pilot"}[1m]))

Rollback & escalation triggers (playbook):
- Pager (SEV) if any of: p95 > 500ms for 5m, error rate > 1.5% for 5m, model quality regression detected against eval set (>2% drop).
- Immediate pause if: repeated 5xxs concentrated in a single model shard or routing path (dominant failure > 60% of errors).
- If capacity unexpectedly saturates (GPU util > 92% sustained > 10m) -> reduce traffic slice to previous stable stage and open incident.

RACI / owners (quick map):
- Product ops (Aisha) — overall rollout lead, OK to pause
- Applied ML (Miguel) — model quality and calibration, owns eval set run
- SRE (Evan) — infra alarms, autoscaling and rollbacks
- Dev (Priya) — deployer, routing rules and feature flags

Quick capacity math (rough):
Assumptions: avg tokens per req = 200, model throughput per A100-equivalent = 60 req/s (mixed), GPUs available=8
Estimated capacity = 8 * 60 = 480 req/s -> headroom for target throughput 600 req/s is low; need to ensure batching gains or increase pool. For pilot we plan to throttle to 450 req/s peak and use backpressure for overflow.

Prelaunch checklist (checked/notes):
- [x] Synthetic eval run completed against held prompt set (owner: Miguel)
- [x] Canary route flag implemented (feature flag + routing weight)
- [x] Dashboards (p50/p95, error rate, cache hit, token burn) created (owner: Priya)
- [ ] Alert runbook drafted (pager steps + slack channel) (owner: Aisha) — IN PROGRESS
- [ ] Regression test runner wired to prod eval pipeline (owner: Miguel)
- [ ] Load test harness to simulate 40% spike (owner: SRE)

Customer communication plan (short):
- Internal beta customers: short heads-up email day -3, FAQ + known limitations.
- Public customers: no change during pilot. Any service impact -> personal outreach from CS.

Open questions & follow-ups:
1) Do we have permission to scale Dedicated pool for the pilot window if metrics show headroom risk? (ask infra procurement)
2) What is acceptable cost delta to finance beyond the +12% pilot target? Need approvals for buffer.
3) Validate whether our trace sampling at 1% is enough to capture anomalous slow-paths; consider increasing to 5% during Stage C.

Next steps (this week):
- Finalize alert runbook and Slack escalation channel (Aisha) — due: 2025-01-24
- Schedule synthetic 10k prompt run and attach output to CONFLUENCE:PRODOPS-RTY-142 (Miguel) — due: 2025-01-20
- SRE to run an autoscaling dry-run in staging mirroring pilot traffic profile (Evan) — due: 2025-01-22

Notes-to-self (rough):
- Watch cache warmup at stage B; we saw a 1.8x latency multiplier last time for first 30 minutes. Might want to pre-warm with synthetic warmed traffic.
- Keep the canary flag gating on both routing weight AND a header check so we can force-route test sessions easily.

Appendix: sample alert text (to copy into alerting tool)
ALERT: Pilot-route p95 latency breach
Summary: p95 latency > 500ms for 5m for pilot-route
Severity: Sev2
Action: Pause rollout, reduce traffic 50%, notify oncall and product ops, run `pilot-rollout/triage` checklist

End notebook.
